title: Manganese Oxide Nanoparticle Synthesis by Thermal Decomposition of Manganese(II) Acetylacetonate
protocol: Assemble glassware and tubing only during the initial setup.
Cover glass connections with a short piece of smaller tubing if there is a mismatch between chemical resistant tubing and connection size.
Secure an air-free nitrogen tank to the wall near a chemical fume hood using approved strap restraints.
Attach a nitrogen regulator to the nitrogen tank.
Fill the gas drying column with desiccant.
Connect chemical resistant tubing from the nitrogen regulator to the bottom inlet of the gas drying column.
Secure the glass manifold containing at least 2 outlet stopcocks to the top of the fume hood using two metal claw clamps.
Attach chemical resistant tubing from the outlet of the gas drying column to the inlet of the manifold.
Place three mineral oil bubblers in the fume hood.
Secure the bubblers using metal claw clamps.
Fill the leftmost bubbler with approximately one inch of silicone oil from the bottom.
Fill the middle bubbler with approximately one and a half inches of silicone oil from the bottom.
Fill the rightmost bubbler with approximately two inches of silicone oil from the bottom.
Connect the outlet on the right stopcock of the manifold to the threaded end of a glass elbow adapter using chemical resistant tubing.
Attach the threaded end of another glass elbow adapter to the inlet of the middle bubbler using chemical resistant tubing.
Connect the outlet of the middle bubbler to the inlet of the leftmost bubbler using chemical resistant tubing.
Connect the outlet on the left stopcock of the manifold to the inlet of the rightmost bubbler.
Place the stir plate in the fume hood.
Put the heating mantle on top of the stir plate.
Secure the middle neck of the round bottom flask with a metal claw clamp.
Add a magnetic stir bar to the round bottom flask.
Place the glass funnel in the middle neck of the round bottom flask.
Check the manifold: ensure the safety stopcock and input stopcock are open.
Weigh 1.51 g of manganese(II) acetylacetonate (Mn(II) ACAC).
Place Mn(II) ACAC inside the round bottom flask using the glass funnel.
Add 20 mL of oleylamine to the round bottom flask using a glass pipette.
Add 40 mL of dibenzyl ether to the round bottom flask using a glass pipette.
Remove the funnel and clean it with hexane.
Attach the condenser to the left neck of the round bottom flask.
Secure the condenser with a metal claw clamp.
Add the glass elbow adapter on top of the condenser.
Connect chemical resistant tubing from the adapter to the middle mineral oil bubbler.
Connect water compatible tubing from the water outlet spout in the fume hood to the inlet of the condenser.
Connect water compatible tubing from the outlet of the condenser to the drain in the fume hood.
Secure the tubing to the condenser connections with interlocked worm gear metal hose clamps.
Add the rotovap trap to the right neck of the round bottom flask.
Place the glass elbow adapter on top of the rotovap trap.
Connect chemical resistant tubing from the adapter to the right stopcock manifold outlet.
Attach the rubber stopper to the middle neck of the round bottom flask and fold it over.

Add four green plastic conical joint clips to secure the connections between glassware: elbow adapter and rotovap trap, rotovap trap and round bottom flask, round bottom flask and condenser, condenser and elbow adapter.
Place the temperature probe into the smallest neck of the round bottom flask, ensuring it is immersed in the fluid mixture but not touching the bottom.
Tighten and secure the temperature probe with a neck cap and o-ring.
Seal the connection between the temperature probe and the glassware using paraffin plastic film.
Connect the temperature probe to the input of the temperature controller.
Connect the heating mantle to the output of the temperature controller.
Turn on the stir plate and start stirring vigorously.
Open the air-free nitrogen tank and slowly begin flowing nitrogen into the system.
Adjust the nitrogen flow until a steady slow stream of bubbles forms in the middle mineral oil bubbler.
Turn on the cold water in the fume hood to the condenser.
Check that no water leaks from the tubing.
Put the sash of the fume hood down before the reaction begins.
Turn on the temperature controller (power and heating supply).
Observe the temperature controller display to confirm the temperature increases from room temperature to 60 °C over 30 min.
Ensure that the temperature controller stabilizes at 60 °C for 1 min as it prepares for a faster heating rate in stage 3.
Check the temperature controller display as the temperature rises to 280 °C at 10 °C per minute over 22 min.
Make sure the water flow through the condenser is sufficient.
Confirm the temperature controller displays a constant reaction temperature of 280 °C for 30 min.
Observe the reaction color change to a green tone, which indicates MnO formation.
Once the reaction reaches 280 °C, turn off the nitrogen tank.
Close the right stopcock for the inlet of the reaction on the manifold.
Keep the safety stopcock open.
Check the temperature controller display to ensure that the heating stops automatically.
Keep the temperature probe inside and wait until the temperature reaches room temperature for nanoparticle collection.
Turn off the temperature controller, the stir plate, and the cold water.
Remove the water-compatible tubing from the condenser, water faucet in the fume hood, and drain.
Remove all plastic conical joint clips from glassware connections.
Remove the glass elbow adapters from the rotovap trap and the condenser.
Secure the elbow adapters to the metal latticework for future use.
Detach the condenser and rotovap trap from the round bottom flask.
Rinse the insides of the condenser and rotovap trap with hexane.
Remove the rubber stopper and temperature probe, clean them with 70% ethanol.
Pour the MnO nanoparticle solution into a clean 500 mL beaker.
Use hexane (~5 mL) to rinse the round bottom flask and add the hexane with residual MnO nanoparticles into the 500 mL beaker.
Note the current volume of the MnO nanoparticle mixture.
Add 200 proof ethanol to the nanoparticle mixture using a volume ratio of 2:1.
Pour the nanoparticle mixture equally into four centrifuge tubes, around 3/4 full.
Centrifuge nanoparticles for 10 min at 17,400 x g at 10 °C.
Discard the supernatant into a waste beaker, being careful not to disturb the pellet.
Add 5 mL of hexane to each centrifuge tube containing MnO nanoparticle pellets.
Resuspend the nanoparticles using a bath sonicator and/or vortex until the solution becomes cloudy and the pellet disappears.
Add more 200 proof ethanol to the centrifuge tubes until 3/4 full.
Repeat steps of adding hexane, resuspending nanoparticles with sonication/vortexing, and adding ethanol until the solution is 3/4 full.
Combine the resuspended nanoparticles from four centrifuge tubes into two centrifuge tubes.
Repeat step of adding hexane, resuspending nanoparticles with sonication/vortexing without additional ethanol addition.
Combine and transfer the MnO nanoparticles resuspended in hexane into a preweighed 20 mL glass scintillation vial.
Leave the lid off to allow the hexane to evaporate overnight in the fume hood.
Transfer the uncovered glass scintillation vial containing dried nanoparticles into a vacuum oven.
Dry out the nanoparticles at 100 °C for 24 hours.
Use a spatula to break up the powder inside the vial once nanoparticles are dried.
Weigh the vial containing dried MnO nanoparticles and subtract the known weight of the glass scintillation vial to determine nanoparticle yield.
Store nanoparticles at room temperature inside the glass scintillation vial with the lid on.
Wrap the lid with paraffin plastic film.
Pulverize the MnO nanoparticles into a thin powder using a mortar and pestle.
Add 5 mg of MnO nanoparticles to a 15 mL conical centrifuge tube.
Add 10 mL of 200 proof ethanol to the nanoparticle mixture.
Bath sonicate the nanoparticle mixture for 5 min or until full resuspension of the nanoparticles.
Add three 5 μL drops of the nanoparticle mixture onto a 300 mesh copper grid support film of carbon type-B.
Let air dry the drops on the copper grid.
Position the grid on the tweezers with the darker side up before adding the drops containing nanoparticles.
Assess nanoparticle shape and size using transmission electron microscopy (TEM).
Apply typical parameters for TEM including a beam strength of 200 kV, a spot size of 1, and a magnification of 300x.
Collect images on areas of the grid containing 10 - 30 evenly distributed nanoparticles.
Avoid collecting images from areas with nanoparticle aggregations.
Image areas from different grid squares to ensure even distribution.
Take between 25 - 30 images per sample for optimal size distribution analysis.
Open a TEM image using File | Open in ImageJ.
Click the straight-line tool and hold Shift to trace the scale bar length.
Click Analyze | Set Scale, enter the true scale measurement in Known distance.
Change the unit of length to nanometers.
Check Global to maintain consistent scaling across all images.
Click OK to confirm the scale settings.
Trace the diameter of a nanoparticle using the straight-line tool.
Click Analyze | Measure or press Ctrl+M for measurements.
Look for the results pop-up window with measurement details.
Confirm that the Length column is present, indicating nanoparticle diameters in nanometers.
Repeat step until all the nanoparticles in the image are sized.
Move to the next image by clicking File | Open Next or using Ctrl+Shift+O keys.
Go to the Results window and click File | Save As after sizing all nanoparticles in all images.
Rename the results file and click Save.
View and analyze all nanoparticle diameters in a spreadsheet program after importing the results file.
Pulverize the MnO nanoparticles into a thin powder using a mortar and pestle.
Place the fine nanoparticle powder into the sample holder using a spatula.
Follow the sample loading procedure for the X-ray diffraction (XRD) machine to be used.
Determine bulk composition of MnO nanoparticles using XRD.
Collect XRD spectra over a 2θ range from 10° to 110°.
Save the generated .XRD file and open it in the XRD analysis program.
Identify all the main peaks in the sample’s measured XRD spectrum by clicking on the IdeAll button in the software.
Select File on the toolbar, followed by Save as… to save the data as an ASC file.
Pattern match the XRD database of known compounds using the program.
Specify anticipated compounds such as manganese and oxygen to narrow the search.
Select Analysis | Search & Match from the menu options.
In the pop-up window, select Chemistry and click on the desired chemical elements.
Choose all relevant chemical elements and then select Search.
Wait for a list of chemical compositions matching the XRD spectrum to appear.
If two or more compositions are chosen, note the composition percentage provided by the program.
Remove the background from the XRD spectrum by clicking the Fit Background button if necessary.
Click Background in the pop-up window after selecting Fit Background.
Subtract the background to refine the spectrum.
Confirm that the refined spectrum starts with 0 on the y-axis.
Save the data again without the background.
Add dry MnO nanoparticle powder to the sample holder for Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) analysis.
Evaluate nanoparticle surface chemistry using FTIR.
Collect FTIR spectra between a 4000 and 400 cm-1 wavelength range with a resolution of 4 cm-1.
Clean the FTIR sample holder and add liquid oleylamine.
Repeat evaluation of nanoparticle surface chemistry using FTIR after adding liquid oleylamine.
Remove background from the collected FTIR spectrum by selecting Transforms in the drop-down menu, followed by Baseline Correct.
Select Linear as the correction type for baseline correction.
Use left mouse click to select baseline points on the original spectrum.
Save the corrected spectrum under another name or replace the old spectrum.
